note: Transcribed exactly. Categories absent here are absent in the spec; the release validator reports them under 9.1(h) rather than inventing coverage.

FM-01.weak_behavior: Labels polished human prose as AI with high confidence

FM-02.weak_behavior: Elevated false positives on populations most harmed by accusation

FM-03.weak_behavior: Boilerplate and verbatim documentation flagged as AI

FM-04.weak_behavior: Keys on em dashes, headers, dated vocabulary and fires

FM-05.weak_behavior: Misses AI generated under style constraints or steered decoding
FM-05.misleading_feature: Burstiness and tell absence read as human

FM-06.weak_behavior: Reads surface noise as proof of humanity and its absence as proof of AI

FM-07.weak_behavior: Forces a binary answer or scores mid-probability without meaning it
FM-07.misleading_feature: Whichever segment dominates the feature window

FM-08.weak_behavior: Content features leak into what should be a process judgment
FM-08.misleading_feature: Topical and lexical overlap with the source

FM-10.weak_behavior: Crashes, NaN, tokenizer explosion, silent truncation, or confident labels on unclassifiable input

FM-11.weak_behavior: An LLM-judge follows instructions embedded in the text under evaluation
FM-11.misleading_feature: Imperative text addressed to the classifier

FM-12.weak_behavior: Sharp accuracy drop on unseen or legacy model families

FM-13.weak_behavior: An LLM judge systematically misclassifies its own family's output
FM-13.misleading_feature: Familiarity of the judge with its own distribution

FM-14.weak_behavior: Performance varies wildly across formats; terse registers degrade to chance without confidence dropping

FM-15.misleading_feature: Any feature at all, over-trusted at short length

FM-16.weak_behavior: Translationese scored as AI regardless of source; code-switched human text flagged
